models.title: Model A: data table
models.note: matches the book's practice task exactly
models.prompt: The table below shows the percentage of households in Algeria with access to selected utilities and technologies in 2005 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

rows: Mobile phone (at least one per household)

modelAnswer: The table shows the proportion of Algerian households with access to five utilities and technologies in 2005 compared with 2025. Overall, access to every item increased over the twenty-year period, although the scale of the increase varied enormously, from a marginal rise in electricity access to a complete transformation in home internet use.

Electricity and piped drinking water were already widespread in 2005, at 97% and 78% of households respectively, and both edged higher by 2025, reaching 99% and 96%. Mobile phone ownership, meanwhile, rose dramatically from 41% to 98% of households, meaning it went from a minority to a near-universal technology over the period.

The most striking change was in home internet access, which climbed from just 4% of households in 2005 to 71% in 2025, by far the largest percentage-point increase of any category. Private car ownership also grew, albeit more modestly, from 22% to 39%, remaining the least widespread item on the list in both years.

whyScoresWell.en: Paraphrases the title (doesn't copy it), gives one overview sentence before any numbers, groups the five rows into sensible comparisons rather than listing every figure in order, uses real numbers as evidence, stays purely descriptive with zero opinion.
whyScoresWell.ar: يعيد صياغة العنوان (لا ينسخه)، يقدّم جملة عامة واحدة قبل ذكر أي أرقام، يجمّع الصفوف الخمسة في مقارنات منطقية بدلاً من سرد كل رقم بالترتيب، يستخدم أرقامًا حقيقية كدليل، ويبقى وصفيًا بحتًا دون أي رأي شخصي.

models.title: Model B: process diagram
models.prompt: The diagram below shows the process by which tap water is treated before it reaches homes. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

stages: Storage and distribution to homes via pipes

modelAnswer: The diagram illustrates the stages involved in treating tap water before it is supplied to households.

Overall, the process consists of six main stages, beginning with raw water collection and ending with distribution to homes, during which impurities are progressively removed and the water is disinfected.

The process begins when water is drawn from a river or reservoir and passed through a screening stage, where large debris such as leaves and sediment is removed. Next, chemicals are added during coagulation, causing fine particles to clump together; these are then allowed to settle out during sedimentation.

Following this, the water is filtered through layers of sand and gravel, which removes any remaining suspended particles. It is then disinfected, typically through the addition of chlorine, to eliminate harmful bacteria and other microorganisms. Finally, the treated water is stored in a holding tank before being distributed to homes through a network of underground pipes.
In summary, the water undergoes a sequence of physical and chemical treatments, moving from a natural source to a safe, drinkable supply delivered directly to consumers.

whyScoresWell.en: Consistent passive voice ("is drawn", "are added"), clear sequence words (begins, next, following this, finally), an overview before the detail, no opinion.
whyScoresWell.ar: استخدام ثابت للمبني للمجهول ("يُسحب"، "تُضاف")، كلمات تسلسل واضحة (يبدأ، بعد ذلك، بعد هذا، أخيرًا)، نظرة عامة قبل التفاصيل، دون أي رأي شخصي.

models.title: Model A: agree or disagree
models.note: matches the book's practice task topic
models.prompt: Many young people today choose to leave their home country to study or work abroad rather than build a career at home. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this trend?
modelAnswer: I largely agree that leaving one's home country for study or work abroad is a reasonable, often necessary choice for young people today, even though it comes at a personal cost.

The strongest argument is economic. In many developing countries, including my own, qualified graduates often face limited job openings, salaries that don't match their qualifications, or bureaucratic barriers to starting a business. Moving abroad often lets a young professional be paid and promoted on actual skill rather than connections, which explains why so many choose this path despite leaving family behind.

This choice is not without drawbacks: emigration can accelerate a "brain drain," and families are separated for years at a time. On balance, I believe the individual's right to pursue better opportunities outweighs the collective cost, provided governments also work to make staying a genuinely competitive option.

whyScoresWell.en: Clear position stated immediately and held throughout (Task Response), one main idea per paragraph with a logical for/against structure (Coherence), precise vocabulary ("brain drain", "bureaucratic barriers") without sounding memorised (Lexical Resource), a mix of simple and complex sentences (Grammar).
whyScoresWell.ar: موقف واضح يُذكر فورًا ويستمر طوال المقال (الاستجابة للمهمة)، فكرة رئيسية واحدة لكل فقرة ببنية منطقية مع/ضد (الترابط والتماسك)، مفردات دقيقة ("هجرة الأدمغة"، "عوائق بيروقراطية") دون أن تبدو محفوظة (الثروة اللغوية)، مزيج من الجمل البسيطة والمركبة (القواعد).

models.title: Model B: discuss both views
models.note: matches the book's practice task exactly
models.prompt: Some people believe that university education should be free for all students, regardless of their family's income. Others believe that students who can afford to pay should do so, so that the money saved can be used to support only the poorest students. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
modelAnswer: There is ongoing debate about how university education should be funded: whether it should be free for every student, or whether only the poorest students should receive support while those who can pay do so. Both positions have genuine merit, though I believe a targeted system of support is the more realistic and fair approach.

Supporters of universal free tuition argue that education is a public good rather than a private privilege, and that charging fees deters capable students from low-income families from applying at all, regardless of how generous the support system looks on paper. They also point out that a country benefits as a whole from a more highly educated population, through higher tax revenue and a more skilled workforce later on, so the investment pays for itself over time.

On the other hand, those who favour means-tested support argue that making every student's education free, including those whose families could easily afford to pay, wastes public money that could instead be concentrated on students who genuinely cannot afford to attend. In a country like Algeria, where public budgets are already stretched across healthcare, infrastructure, and other priorities, directing limited funds toward the students who need them most arguably produces a fairer and more sustainable outcome than spreading the same budget thinly across everyone.

In my view, the second approach is more practical, provided that the system for determining who can and cannot afford to pay is transparent and genuinely accessible, rather than discouraging eligible students through complicated paperwork. Free education for all sounds appealing in principle, but in a context of limited public funds, means-tested support is more likely to reach the students whose access to university genuinely depends on it.
Governments should therefore prioritise targeted financial support over universal free tuition, while working to keep the application process for that support as simple as possible.

whyScoresWell.en: Addresses exactly what "discuss both views and give your own opinion" requires: covers each side in its own paragraph before stating a position, uses precise vocabulary ("means-tested", "public good"), ties the conclusion to the Algerian context without losing the general argument, and never drifts off-topic into unrelated issues.
whyScoresWell.ar: يستجيب بدقة لما تتطلبه عبارة "ناقش الرأيين وأبدِ رأيك": يغطي كل رأي في فقرة منفصلة قبل تحديد الموقف، يستخدم مفردات دقيقة ("دعم موجّه حسب الدخل"، "منفعة عامة")، يربط الخاتمة بالسياق الجزائري دون فقدان الحجة العامة، ولا يحيد عن الموضوع أبدًا.
